Commentary.Commentary: The visitors hold the upper hand as things stand and it'll take something special from Zimbabwe to turn things around. Don't go anywhere as the final innings will be starting in a very short while.

A stat that will please the fans of Zimbabwe though. The spinners for the home side have never taken as many wickets as they have in this particular Test. They have taken 16 wickets, the previous best was 15 against New Zealand at the same venue in 1997.

It was a decent bowling effort from the home side. The spin attack of Graeme Cremer and Sean Williams led the way with the others playing their part in this. Could have been different had they taken their chances. Now, there are two full days left in this game, and with a record target of 434 to chase down, it's safe to say it won't be a cakewalk by any means.

The ideal start to the day for Zimbabwe in all honesty. They've managed to scalp the remaining West Indian wickets in less than 4 overs. The main focus when play began was whether Roston Chase could get to what would have been a well-deserved ton, and he eventually couldn't get there. Jason Holder won't mind that at all though, they have more than enough on the board and will be raring to have a go at the Zimbabweans.

OUT! What was the hurry, Roston Chase? The hundred was there for the taking but he has thrown it away. The field placement has brought about this rash shot from the batter. Cremer blocked all the single-taking options and Chase didn't want Gabriel to face the next over. Hence, he decides to take matters in his own hands and tries to go big. Williams invites him to do so by tossing it up around middle and leg, Chase clears his front leg and looks to go downtown but is in no position to do so. Misses the ball completely and loses his leg stick. The hosts are ecstatic and Williams celebrates like an airplane taking off. A good knock comes to an end, although Roston will be kicking himself. WINDIES FOLD UP FOR 373!
Flatter around off, punched towards covers.
This ball is cut away towards point.
Floated outside off, Chase goes for an ugly slog across the line but ends up missing the ball completely. The ball lobs off the keeper's gloves and goes over the slips. No run though.
This is bowled outside off, Roston lets it go.
Fuller around off, driven towards covers.
Bowled on the pads, Gabriel misses the defense. The ball lobs off his pads towards fine leg.
Gabriel has his bat and pad close together and defends it by striding forward.
Shannon lunges forward and blocks.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
This ball is punched off the back foot through covers. Chase takes a single and leaves the no. 11 to face the last four balls.
Flatter on the pads, Chase lunges to defend but the ball takes the inner half and rolls towards fine leg. A couple of runs taken.
Gabriel strides forward but gets an outside edge towards slip. He is safe and sound!
This is bowled outside off, Gabriel fails to get bat to that.
A tad shorter around off, Chase goes back and pulls it through square leg for a run. Now Gabriel has to negotiate the last two balls of the over.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Chase goes back and punches it towards covers.
Chase misjudges this! Williams floats it outside off, Roston thinks that it would spin away and leaves it alone. The ball goes straight on and passes close to the pads.
Sean Williams to bowl from the other end. He'll be bowling to Roston Chase. Let's see what happens here. Just the lone slip in place...

Almost a replica of Dominica! Cremer floats it outside off, Gabriel is a free man, is confident of his skills and wants to play a big shot. He has a full go at this one and gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket. Chase would have had his heart in his mouth there. He was at the receiving end when West Indies almost saved the Test against Pakistan, only for Gabriel to go for an unwanted glory shot. Entertaining for the rest but not for the Windies, one thinks.

Not Out! A review wasted for a milestone. Cremer in pursuit of a hat-trick, floats it outside leg, the ball spins in a touch. Gabriel looks to clip it away but misses and gets hit on the back pad. The home side players appeal but the umpire stays unmoved. After some thought, Cremer opts to go for the DRS. Replays show that the ball pitched well outside leg. The hosts lose a review and Chase still has a chance to get to his milestone as Gabriel stays on.
Review! Graeme Cremer has caught Shannon Gabriel leg before and reviewed it immediately. Doesn't look out at all but you can't really blame him for doing so.

Shannon Gabriel is the last man in for the Windies. He comes out to face the hat-trick ball. Andy Blignaut is the only Zimbabwean to take a hat-trick in Tests against Bangladesh in 2004. Can Cremer become the second one today?

OUT! What a start for Zimbabwe and Cremer! He's on a hat-trick yet again in this Test! He loops a googly around off and middle, Roach, the tailender that he is, fails to pick that up. Lunges forward to play for the leg spin but ends up missing the ball and his stumps get disturbed. Can Chase get to his ton now?

It's a beautiful day for a game of cricket. Everybody is set for the play to get underway. Quick runs or quick wickets, what do you think will happen this morning? Will Roston Chase get to his ton? Will West Indies declare after that? He strides out to the center and he has the new batsman Kemar Roach for company. Graeme Cremer will begin with the ball for the hosts. A slip in place.

Tino Mawoyo doing the pitch report, says that the pitch has degraded a lot more and it has become a lot drier. The area around the good length is the critical one, he opines. Walking to the other end, he states that the spinners could get a lot of purchase towards the City End as the cracks there have opened up a bit more. There is a big crater outside the left hander's off stump area and he reckons that leg spinners have a vital role there.

Hello everybody! We welcome you to our coverage of Day 4 of the first Test between Zimbabwe and Windies in Bulawayo. Roston Chase is 9 away from what would be his fourth Test ton. Thus, we can expect the visitors to continue to bat for at least an hour or so. The hosts already have a tough task on hand as they will be in pursuit of the highest run-chase in this format. Their aim first up would be to deny easy runs to the opposition. Will they be able to do so though? Stay with us to find out.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Zimbabwe were guilty of having lapses on the field. They handed two lives to Brathwaite early in the day which helped the tourists march ahead with the lead. The home side's bowlers weren't too bad but they couldn't be penetrative enough to strike crucial blows to the opposition. It will be interesting to see whether the visitors declare overnight or bat for some more time before charging in with the ball. That's it from us today. Do join us tomorrow at 1000 local (0800 GMT) for what could be an attritional day of Test cricket. Till then, goodbye and take care.

A grinding day's play! Although Windies have taken a lead of 429, they have crawled their way there. Chase made use of the opportunity to notch up his 4th fifty in Tests. He did hurry up towards the end but couldn't get to his ton today. Only time will tell if he does get a chance to complete it. Bishoo came to the party and scored some vital runs to hurt the opposition further. Earlier, the away side was helped by grinding knocks from Brathwaite and Shai Hope. Both of them missed their milestones by a narrow margin.

OUT! One too many! Greediness consumes Bishoo. Cremer tosses it up around off, Devendra gets down to slog it over deep mid-wicket but finds Williams stationed there. He nailed the shot but unfortunately found the fielder. Won't get a fifty and goes for 44, his second-best Test score. End of a good knock from him though. THAT'S STUMPS, DAY 3!
FOUR! Bishoo doesn't care even if it is the last over of the day. He sees the flight offered by Cremer, gets down and hits it over square leg for a boundary.
Bowls it flatter on the stumps, Bishoo stays in the crease and defends it.
Last over of the day! Graeme Cremer will bowl it. A slip, leg slip and a short leg in position.
Floated outside off, Chase looks to defend but misses.
Tossed up around off, Roston lunges forward and defends.
Served in line of the stumps, defended from the crease showing the full bat face.
This ball is kept out from within the crease.

Sharp turn but well negotiated by Bishoo. Williams tosses it outside off, the ball spins into the batsman. Devendra goes back and misses the flick but gets it off the pads towards backward square leg for a leg bye.
Fired around off, Bishoo goes back and plays it towards cover-point.
This ball is pushed off the back foot towards mid off.
FOUR! Chase moves into the 90s! Slower off cutter around off, Chase picks up the variation early. Hits it over mid-wicket. The ball lands near the fence and eventually trickles to the ropes.
Similar delivery around off, Chase drives it straight back. The bowler sways away from it, the mid off fielder dives but can't stop and eventually mid on does so.
Fuller outside off, pushed towards covers from the crease.
Edged but falls short! Jarvis bangs it short around leg, Chase hops and looks to nudge it fine but gets some glove. The ball fell just short of the diving Chakabva.
On a length around middle and leg, Chase stands tall and pushes it down the ground. Mid on cuts it off. No run there.
FOUR! Enough of blocking for Bishoo! Williams loops it up around off, the southpaw gets down and hits it straight over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Darted outside off, Chase plays it through point and crosses over to the other end.
Floated around off, swept away through square leg for one.
Bowled from over the wicket, Bishoo lunges forward to defend it solidly.

Williams bowls it short from wide of the crease. The well-set Chase has ample time to go back and hit it through mid-wicket. Mpofu chases it down and parries it to Taylor who runs after him. The batsmen get three before the ball is back to the keeper.
Floats it around middle and leg, Chase lunges forward and defends it solidly.
Sean Williams back on. Will he able to add another to his kitty?
On a length around off, the batsman stands tall and blocks it towards covers.
Jarvis comes round the wicket and spears it full around off. Bishoo flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Chase punches this delivery through cover-point for a single.
Hurled outside off, Roston doesn't bother putting bat to it.

Fazeer Mohammed opines that how much ever people talk about being selfish in achieving individual records, this game is about that too and it isn't wrong. If there is time, why not aim for individual records, he argues, as eventually that's what we end up talking about.
This delivery is flicked off his pads towards mid-wicket.
Bowled around off, Chase stays in the crease and defends it with a straight bat.
Flatter on the stumps, Devendra goes back to negotiate it safely.
Cremer comes round the wicket now and bowls it fuller outside off, Bishoo drives it against the spin to covers.
Landed around off, Chase punches it through cover-point for one run.
This delivery is flicked away through backward square leg for a run.
Floated full outside off, Bishoo clears his front leg and hits it to mid on.
Looped up around middle and leg, Bishoo gets forward to smother the spin.
Hurled around off, Chase defends it from the crease.
On a length outside off, Chase guides it towards gully.
FOUR! The message from the dressing room seems to be clear. Chase looks to be in a hurry to get to his ton. He takes the aerial route and hits it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
This ball is driven towards the fielder at mid off.

FOUR! Not a soul moved there! It's full and wide, Chase stays where he is and absolutely creams it through covers. The ball speeds away to the boundary. Nobody bothered moving. You don't see him play these shots often but now he is doing so. Playing according to the situation.
Jarvis bowls it fuller around off, Chase drives it off the inside half towards mid on.
Holder is in his whites. Is a declaration imminent? We don't know. There are two days left in the game, there is no hurry in terms of time.
Kyle Jarvis is back on. One final throw of the dice from Zimbabwe?
Bowled around off and middle, Bishoo blocks it solidly.
Bishoo crouches low to dead-bat it on the ground.
Windies lead by 400! Chase continues his single-taking game by collecting one after driving it towards long on. Wonder how much more do they want, before they'd insert the opposition in.

So near yet so far! Cremer tosses it outside off, Bishoo gets down and looks to sweep. Gets an inside edge onto his pads and the ball rolls through the keeper's legs. The batsmen cross over for a run.
Graeme continues over the wicket to the southpaw and bowls it around middle and leg. Bishoo blocks it off the front foot.
Sharp turn on that delivery that is pitched outside off. Chase is well set for that to not trouble him. Taps it towards third man for a single.
Tossed up around off, defended towards silly point.
Similar delivery and sequence of actions like the previous delivery.
Raza flights this more around off, Bishoo strides forward to bury it onto the ground.
Now this ball is pushed towards long on for one.
Served around off, Chase pushes it off the front foot towards the bowler.
Chase rocks back and pushes it towards mid-wicket.

Ian Bishop makes a superb point on-air that it should be perfectly fine if the ball is spinning from ball one. It just needs to be consistent and unless it is dangerous (meaning extravagant and crumbling on the first few days itself), there should not be any problem. Don't think many will agree with this unpopular opinion.
A forward defense exhibited to this delivery around off.
Devendra punches this towards covers.
Straighter ball outside off, Bishoo goes back and presents a straight bat to defend it.
Loopy delivery around off, he lunges forward and bunts it onto the ground.
Bishoo stays in his crease and defends it.
SIX! It's Bishoo, his favourite mode and his favourite area. Cremer floats it around off, Devendra gets down and takes the aerial route over deep mid-wicket. The ball goes all the way.
Fired on the pads, Chase looks to flick but gets a thin edge towards fine leg. He gets a brace there.
Bishoo punches it off the back foot towards mid off for a run.

Lovely committed effort by the fielder there. Raza serves a full loopy ball outside off, Roston drives it towards wide mid off. Jarvis runs to his left, dives and keeps the batsmen down to one. 50-run stand between these two. They are doing well to push the lead up.
This delivery is punched back to the bowler.
Similar delivery, Roston goes back and clips it past short leg.
Tossed up around off, Chase camps back and punches it to mid-wicket.
And Chase continues his one-run game. He drives it towards long off and crosses over to the other end.
Bishoo goes aerial again. Occasionally he keeps doing it and is effective too. This time he pulls it over mid-wicket. Mire runs to his right and restricts the batsmen to three.
Bishoo gets forward and presents a straight bat as he blocks that.
Landed around off, driven to long off for a run by Roston.
Looped outside off, the ball bounces a tad more. Bishoo goes back, watches it closely and guides it towards backward point for a run.
Floated full around off, Chase drives it to long off for a single.
Flatter outside off, Bishoo punches it towards covers.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Bishoo lunges forward and defends it with a straight bat.
Dropped a tad short outside off, Devendra cuts it to the fielder at point.

Ian Bishop on-air talks about the batting stance of Roston Chase as opposed to Jermaine Blackwood, who gets stumped out often. He spots that Chase's back foot is pretty much inside the crease while Blackwood's back foot is nearly on the crease. It might be a small margin but it leads to Chase still being in the crease even when he is beaten but Blackwood gets outside the crease with the lunge. So maybe Jermaine can learn something by watching Roston bat.
Bishoo strides forward and defends it off the front foot.
Landed around off, Bishoo stays back to bunt that.
Floated outside off, Chase finds covers with the drive.
Served in line of the stumps, Chase goes back and plays it to short leg.
Tossed up leg spinner around off, Bishoo leans forward and pushes it towards mid on. Hares over to get to the other end and does so with ease.
A tad shorter on the stumps, Chase goes back and works it down to long on for one run.
Fuller around off, Roston drives it back to where it came from.
Cremer delivers a gentle floater around off, Chase lunges forward and blocks.

Drinks are on the field now. Zimbabwe have toiled hard without much success apart from Holder's wicket. They need some spark to trigger a batting collapse. The Caribbean side would be happy with how they are placed right now.
Chase drives it through covers to collect a single and retain strike.
This ball is flicked round the corner for nothing.

This is a quicker one pushed with the index finger. Bishoo looks to paddle it but gets an inside edge onto the pads. There is a shout for LBW but the umpire shows no interest. The ball rolls towards backward square leg for a run.
Landed around off, Devendra stays in his crease and bunts it.
Flatter on the pads, worked away towards fine leg for one.
FOUR! Wow! Chase is on top of his game at the moment and he won't miss to score off the bad balls. Raza bowls it full and wide of off, Chase smashes it through covers and helps himself to a boundary.
Chase collects a single driving it to long off.
A tad shorter around off, Bishoo taps it towards short third man. The slip fielder runs to retrieve that. A run taken.
Served in line of the stumps, Devendra gets nicely forward to bunt it.
Bishoo pushes it from the crease towards covers.
Floated around leg, Devendra lunges forward and buries it into the ground.
A low full toss around leg. Chase wrists it to long on and crosses over. Actually, it was a variation by Cremer but didn't come off as expected.
This ball is turned towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Similar delivery, Roston goes back and taps it towards short third man.
Flatter in line of the stumps, Chase gets back to block it.
Gets forward and pushes this down to long on for one run.

FOUR! Bishoo belts that! He's looking to get some runs under his belt without worrying about the threat of the pitch. Flighted delivery around off, he gets down and slogs it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Floated around off and middle, Bishoo goes back and defends it watchfully.
Loopy ball around off, swept away through backward square leg for one run.
Floated around off, the batter turns it towards square leg.
Bishoo works this just past short leg for nothing.
300 up for Windies now. Bowled on the pads, Chase works it towards fine leg for a run.
Served outside off, Chase looks to cut but chops it on the keeper's pads. The Zimbabweans wonder why didn't it disturb the timber behind!
Landed around off, Bishoo drives it through covers for a single.
Graeme Cremer gets a change of ends.
Fired flatter outside off, Bishoo camps back and cuts it. Gets it off the outer half towards third man. Taylor from backward point chases it down and saves a run for his side.
Lovely delivery. Tossed up outside off, Bishoo is drawn forward in defense. The ball spins away to beat the outside edge and lands in the keeper's gloves.
Devendra stays in the crease and slaps it straight to the man at covers.
Bishoo stays in the crease and defends it with a straight bat.
Flatter outside off, Bishoo slaps it to the fielder at cover.
Comes in and bowls round the wicket and floats it around leg. Chase flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Sikandar Raza is brought back to bowl. He has a slip and a forward short leg in place.
Full toss by Williams, Chase drives it through mid off for a single.
Floats it outside off, Chase comes forward and blocks it.
Flatter outside off, punched towards point from the crease.
Turns one through backward square leg for a single.
Flatter around off, Bishoo looks to turn it through the leg side but is hit on his pads.
Drives it through mid off for a single.
4th Test fifty for Chase! Goes back and punches one towards long off for a single. He had a tough time in England but has come back in form in time.
Fuller around middle, driven towards covers.
Flatter around leg, nudged off the pads towards backward square leg. A leg bye taken.
Loops it outside off, Bishoo comes forward to defend but gets beaten. The ball goes through the legs of the keeper towards third man. Two runs taken. Byes signaled.
FOUR! Just over! Short from Cremer around off, Bishoo goes back and pulls it over mid-wicket. Just over the man at deep mid-wicket and into the fence. He himself was surprised.
Fuller outside off, Bishoo aims to slog it away but gets it towards short mid-wicket.
Edged! Flatter around middle, Bishoo aims to defend but gets it off the inside edge towards square leg from the crease.
Nudges one through mid on for a single to rotate strike.
Kneels down and sweeps it through square leg for a single.
Stays back in the crease and blocks it.
Bishoo comes forward and drives it through wide mid off. Mpofu saves a boundary with a dive but the batsmen take two runs.
Turns it through mid on for a single.

Woah! Cremer bowls it outside off, the ball comes into Bishoo like a plane taking off flat off the surface. Devendra is hit on his pads as he cannot clip it. Cannot fault him one bit. Bishoo will remember this when he bowls though.
Fuller around middle, pushed towards covers by the batsman.
Flatter around middle, Bishoo lunges forward and turns it towards the on side.
Stays back to this short one and pats it back down the wicket.
Devendra Bishoo is the new man in.

OUT! Cremer has his revenge! Floats it around off, Holder looks to go over covers but gets an outside edge towards backward point. Mpofu takes the catch and celebrates it. Jason was looking to go big but now has to go back to the hut. The lead for West Indies is 337 runs.
FOUR! Googly picked and smacked! Fuller around off and middle, Holder comes forward and launches it over the mid on region for a boundary. That was always coming.
Graeme Cremer comes back on for a bowl.
Flatter around middle, Chase looks to turn it away but gets hit on his back pad.
Pushes it through mid off for a single.
Angles it around middle, Holder comes forward and blocks it.
Shorter around middle, Chase goes back and punches it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Edged! Floats it around off, Holder looks to defend but gets an outside edge towards third man for a single.
Stays back and turns it towards short leg from his crease.
Good length around off, Chase comes forward and defends it.
Good length outside off, played towards deep point for a couple of runs. The throw is flat and on the stumps by the fielder. Mpofu has a good arm but the batsman had got in by then. Two runs taken.
Chase gets across a tad and clips it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Good length around off, Holder comes down and turns it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Edged? Nope! Good length outside off, Holder shapes to defend but gets beaten on the inside edge. The ball goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Fuller outside off, Holder backs away and smacks it towards mid off.
Fuller around middle, driven to long off for a single.
Shorter from wider of the crease, Holder goes back to turn it through mid-wicket but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Fuller around off, defended carefully by Holder.
Lands it around off, Holder comes forward and defends it towards the leg side off the inner half.
Quicker around leg, Jason is awake to it and blocks it watchfully.
TURN! Lands it around leg, spins across Holder who stays back and defends it.
Good length around off, Roston keeps it out.
Length ball outside off, Chase comes forward and pushes it towards covers.
Good length outside off, defended watchfully.
Fuller outside off, Chase looks to drive on the up but is beaten all ends up.
Chase stays back and defends this one watchfully.

Good stop! Fuller in length around middle, Holder just presents it the full face of the bat and gets it through mid on. Cremer gives it a chase and looks to stop the ball near the fence. The umpires are not sure and hence refer it upstairs. Replays show the skipper was just fine. Three runs taken.
Touch short outside off, slapped down towards wide long off for a run.
Plays it before the ball can turn. It's nicely driven past Graeme Cremer at covers who puts in a sloppy effort and a couple of runs are taken.
Coming in and then turning away on off, Jason Holder comes forward and blocks.
Shortens his length on this occasion, pitches it outside off, Roston goes back and cuts it to deep point for a single.
Full and wide outside off, Chase drives it square and finds the man at point.
Darts it very wide outside off, spins away, Chase leaves it alone.
Good length around off, turned towards wide mid on for a single.
Full again, driven again, to mid off but for no runs.
Comes forward and drives it nicely towards mid off.
Fuller outside off, Chase comes forward and drives it towards extra cover.
Shorter in length around middle, Chase pulls it through backward square leg. Waller does well in the deep to stop it from going through. Two runs taken.
Good length outside off, Chase stands tall and defends it.
Kyle Jarvis to bowl from the other end. Think the intent from Holder has something to do with this change. Just guessing though....
Flatter outside off, Holder stands tall and blocks it.
Fuller outside off, Holder drives it on the bounce to Cremer at covers. He takes the ball and celebrates to fool the crowd. He can't fool us though.
FOUR! More runs! Williams floats it outside off, Holder comes forward and drives it through covers for a boundary. He is on 10 in just 2 balls.

SIX! Holder announces his arrival! Fuller outside off, Holder comes forward and just lofts it over the long off region. The ball flies over the fence for a biggie. Does not matter if it's just the first ball, he has shown his intent already.

Welcome for the final session of the day's play! Jason Holder joins Roston Chase at the crease. Zimbabwe's mindset will be of restriction while Windies would look for runs. Sean Williams will complete his over.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

Zimbabwe wouldn't be overly satisfied as in spite of help from the deck, their returns are pretty pedestrian. Jarvis had a good spell with the second new ball and so did Williams. Post tea, the visitors could probably come out with a mindset of declaring and look to put the game beyond the hosts. The home side would want to restrict them below 350. Do join us in a while for the last session of the day.

A moving session! 89/4 in this second period of play. Windies still have their noses ahead as they have a healthy lead of 304 runs. Brathwaite played a wonderful knock but missed out on a deserving ton. His stand with Shai Hope acted as a catalyst in pushing the lead up.

OUT! Dowrich fails again! Williams loops it around off, Dowrich pushes at it with hard hands. The ball takes the outside edge and flies towards first slip. Masakadza takes the catch bending low. That is another wicket for Sean. He has done his bit to keep his side in the game. Dowrich's poor run in Test cricket continues, which is a shame since he was looking really good.
Flatter around off, Dowrich goes back and chops it towards point from his crease.

Nice timing! Cremer floats it outside off, Dowrich does not mind and hence drives it through wide mid off. Jarvis does well to keep the ball in play, haring after it from mid off. Saves a run for his side.
Floats it around off, Shane blocks it coming forward.
Loops it around off, Dowrich gets in line and keeps it out.

A stat that Jermaine Blackwood wouldn't be proud of - He has been stumped 4 times in his last 7 innings. He needs to be careful with his back foot as he often slides it out and doesn't plant it back in time.
FOUR! Top, top shot! Floats it outside off, Dowrich gets to the pitch of it and creams it through covers. Cremer is leaking runs here. The lead is now over 300! Advantage West Indies!
Flatter around leg, Chase works it through square leg for a single.
Lands it around middle, Roston goes back and defends it.
Quicker around leg, Dowrich shapes to clip it through the leg side but is hit on his back leg. Stifled appeal turned down.
Shorter this time, Dowrich stays back and punches it towards covers.
Angles it around middle and leg, Shane is right forward and blocks it.
Dowrich comes ahead and turns it towards short leg.

In the air but safe! Flatter around off, Dowrich is beaten by the extra bounce and checks his defensive shot at the last moment. The ball pops off the bat and falls short of the short mid-wicket fielder.
Bowls it around leg, spins away, Dowrich does well to keep it out.
Lands the googly around off, turned through mid on for a single.
Roston Chase did work in the nets today before the start of play on his sweep shot, informs Ian Bishop on air. He's played that on the field and it is coming off pretty well here.
Fuller around off, Shane comes forward and blocks it.
Dowrich comes right forward and blocks it.
Bowls it around off, goes straight on, Dowrich leaves it but the ball goes straight on and narrowly misses the stumps.
Turns it towards mid on for a single.
SIX! Up and over! Cremer floats it outside off, Chase gets under it and just launches it over long off for a maximum. Clean strike, that.
Graeme Cremer calls himself back on.
Fuller around off, Shane comes forward and defends it.
FOUR! Off the mark! Shorter around middle, Dowrich goes back in his crease and punches it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Good start for him.
Shane Dowrich strides out to bat.

OUT! Blackwood is a goner! Williams angles it around off, Blackwood shapes to defend it from his crease but is beaten. The keeper takes the bails off and appeals. He does not look too confident though. The third umpire is referred. Replays find Blackwood's back foot is not behind the line and hence, Jermaine has to walk back to the hut. Twice in the game, he has been stumped. He should be kicking himself. Replays show that Jermaine did not attempt to get back in the crease. Ordinary stuff. The change in bowling has worked.
A stumping appeal against Jermaine Blackwood is referred upstairs by the square leg umpire.
Fuller outside off, gets it to turn and bounce a touch more, Blackwood lets it go through.
Shorter outside off, Chase punches it towards point. Mire fumbles and allows a single.
FOUR! Cannot take wickets with such balls. Williams darts it too full and around leg, Chase sweeps it through backward square leg for a boundary. Gift from Sean, that.
Time for some spin. Sean Williams returns for a bowl. He has bowled well without much luck. Time for a change of fortunes?
Fuller around middle and leg, clipped towards long leg for a single.
FOUR! Thumped! Short and wide outside off, Chase gets in position and pumps it past point for a boundary.
Shorter outside off, punched towards mid off by Blackwood for a single.
See, we told you. Length ball from Jarvis, Blackwood gets across and just flicks it over mid-wicket. The slow outfield means that the ball slows down near the ropes. Two runs taken.
Back of a length outside off, comes in, turned towards mid-wicket from the crease.
Jermaine Blackwood comes out to bat. There is no doubt as to how he will bat here.

OUT! Jarvis strikes in time! Angles it around off on a length, gets it to come back in sharply, Hope hops a touch and looks to clip it through but is hit on his pad. The players appeal and the umpire upholds it. Hope is not sure and has a word with his partner. Goes for the review as he must be thinking since he had jumped a touch, the ball could be missing the stumps. Ball Tracker shows three reds and hence Shai has to depart. Handy knock by him. The lead is 271 runs.
Review time! Shai Hope is caught leg before and he's decided to take it upstairs. Looks close to the naked eye. Over to the third umpire now...
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Angling down leg, Chase punishes this without a second's hesitation. Just helps it on its way across the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Fraction straight in line, Hope works it fine down the leg side and takes one.
Full ball outside off, driven down towards mid off.
Short and wide outside off, Hope flays at it but ends up missing it. He'll feel hard done by it, should have put it away.
Yorker fired in on middle, Hope does well to bring his bat down in time and keep it at bay.
FOUR! Slightly overpitched and that's been punished! Shot. Full outside off, Chase elegantly drives it through the gap in the covers and ends the over with a boundary.
Straightening up from around off, Chase leans across to get behind the line and defends it down. Kept the elbow high and kept it out with a good technique.
Short delivery on middle stump, pulled aerially through backward square leg for a single.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
Fullish in length and attacking the stumps, Hope keeps it out with a straight bat.
Keeping a bit low on middle stump, Shai Hope turns it to the mid-wicket area.
Roston Chase has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Huge lbw shout! Full and angling down, catches Chase looks to whip it away on the leg side but gets rapped low on the pads. Mpofu turns and asks the question, but the umpire says nothing. It was always angling down the leg side, so good decision to not review.
Good length delivery in the off stump channel, stands tall and punches it square on the off side.
A firm drive but it's straight to the fielder. Chase connects well but finds the man at cover.
Angling in from a length around off, straightening up off the deck, Roston Chase confidently blocks it down on the off side.
Moving away from outside off, left alone.
Driven to mid off from the front foot. End of a decent over from Jarvis.
Leans ahead a touch to this fullish length ball and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Full ball just outside off, shaping away, Hope mistimes the drive down to mid off.
Back of a length again but this time with width outside off, Hope cuts it hard through cover-point. Picks up a couple of runs as Raza chases it down and pulls it back just inside the rope.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Back of a length delivery outside off, with an open face Hope dabs it to gully.
Short of a good length on middle and off, Roston rises on his toes and pulls it along the ground through square leg for two.
Good length ball outside off, cracked hard to the man at point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Brings it in closer this time, but it's still not close enough as Chase shoulders his arms to it.
Wider outside off this time, another one left alone.
Some seam movement for Mpofu but the line is quite wide. Not enough to make Roston Chase play at it.
Chris Mpofu to bowl now. He'll be sharing the second new ball with Kyle Jarvis.
Angling in at first but then straightening up a shade, Shai Hope comfortably plays it down right under his nose.
Keeps it on the fuller side, well outside off, no trouble for the batsman to let it be.
Fuller length delivery on the fifth stump line, Hope comes forward, reaches out to it and blocks.
FOUR! Too full, too straight and he's paid the price for it. Shai Hope just has to get something on it and he gets enough. Tickles it fine down the leg side and sends it across the fine leg fence.
Short of a good length coming back into the body, Hope looks to work it away on the off side but gets it off the inner half towards mid on.
A completely different sound off the bat with the new ball. Jarvis with a back of a length delivery which zips off the deck, Hope hops and defends it off the outer half in front of point.
Kyle Jarvis back on for another spell. The second new ball has been taken and he will be the first one to have a go with it. Two slips and a gully in place.
Full and flat, not much turn on this occasion, driven straight back to the bowler.
Spinning away a shade around off, defended down on the track from inside the crease.
Bit short again, quicker through the air outside off, dabbed away from the body down to third man for two more.
On a flatter trajectory on leg, Roston Chase goes back and whips it through mid-wicket for a double.
Tossed up on middle and off, Chase clears his front leg and drives it to cover.
Drifting on middle and leg, Chase works it around his pads just wide of short leg.
Drinks are on the field!
Hangs back inside the crease and ensures to end the over without any damage.
Floated on middle and leg, driven down to long on for a run.
Brings the wrists into the play and flicks it well to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has worked it off his pads behind square on the leg side.
Floated on the leg stump line again, tucked towards short fine leg.
On the pads, flicked past short leg.
Spinning away a touch, around off, Chase hangs back and defends it down beside him on the off side.
Short and a bit wide outside off, Roston Chase with a back foot defense in response.
A lot of loop on this, full in length, pushed back to the bowler.
Darted wide outside off, Roston reaches out to it and dabs it late down towards third man. Picks up a couple for doing so.

Turning and bouncing from around off, Hope rocks back and cuts it square of the wicket on the off side. Solomon Mire gives it a long chase and does well to just about pull it back inside the rope. Great effort, saves a run for his side.
Some bite off the surface as Williams bowls it on off, Hope closes the face a bit too early and spoons a leading edge which falls safely a bit square on the off side.
Loopy full delivery on middle, Chase plays it back to Raza.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. Another dot.
Wristed away on the leg side for no run at all.
Full and straight from Raza, Chase stoutly blocks it out.
Touch short, Shai off his back foot punches it down to long on for one.
Full delivery going across, Hope drives it square through cover-point and comes back for the second.
Just enough turn for Williams. Chase is almost undone. Around off, spins ever so slightly and beats the outside edge of the bat.
Plants his front foot forward and meets the ball at its pitch. Places it to the covers for no run.
Minimal spin on it, around the off stick, kept out off the back foot.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
A lot of air on this, draws Chase forward who plays the expansive drive, only to find the cover fielder.
Short, flat and spinning away, Chase waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it down to third man for a brace.
Shai Hope leans ahead to this full delivery and works it to the right of the bowler to end the over.
Flight on this as it's pitched outside off, eased away to the covers.
Loopy and full outside off, Hope drives it a bit square, wide of sweeper cover for a couple of good runs.
Chase is off the mark without wasting any time. He goes deep within his crease and whips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Roston Chase is next in to bat.

OUT! Raza has his man! Kraigg Brathwaite is dismissed after being given two lives. Raza continues from around the wicket and floats it up around off, it spins in as Brathwaite moves across to block. Is caught flush in front of the stumps and the umpire has no trouble at all to raise his finger in response to the lbw appeal. Kraigg didn't even bother thinking of reviewing that, it was that clear. Brathwaite departs, but has made a significant contribution with his 86 on a difficult batting track. Excellent knock. Zimbabwe have their breakthrough here, can they make further inroads from this point?
Turning in on middle and leg, worked past short leg.
Hope chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Slider around off, the batsman presents a front foot defense.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Lands it short and around off, Kraigg meets it with a cut and places it to cover.
Spinning away from outside off, left alone.
Superb delivery! Bowls it slower through the air and lands it around off, it spins away and beats the outside edge of Kraigg Brathwaite's bat.
Sean Williams is back on to roll his arm over.
Bowls this across outside off, Hope drives it firmly through the covers for a couple of runs.
Turning into the batsman from middle stump, worked away to backward square leg.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Spinning down leg, tucked just wide of short fine leg for a single.
Sprays it on the pads, worked away with soft hands on the on side.
FOUR! Short, flat and down the leg side, Brathwaite has all the time in the world to put this away. He pulls it through backward square leg and gets a boundary to his name.
Skidding off the deck a bit outside off, off the outer half Hope defends.
Full outside off, driven again this time a bit harder to the cover fielder.
Slower through the air, around off, pushed away in front of covers.
Flatter and quicker on off, Hope wrists it away nicely towards the mid-wicket area.
Another googly, Hope once again goes back and defends it out off the back foot.
Googly on off, spins in sharply and almost takes Shai Hope by surprise. He adjusts, goes back and nudges it down to short fine leg.
Comes well forward to this fuller length ball and blocks.
Easily flicked away past the short leg fielder.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On leg stump once more, worked behind square leg for nothing.
Straighter in line on middle and leg, Kraigg takes a big lunge forward before defending it back down the track.
On the leg stump line, nudged towards short fine leg for no run.
Googly around off, Shai waits for the ball to come to him before blocking it out.
Hangs back and meets it with the full face of the bat.

Shorter on middle and off, Hope goes back and wrists it towards mid-wicket. His partner wants the run but he immediately shouts 'NO' and sends him back. Good call, the fielder got to the ball rather quickly.
Tossed up on middle, Hope clears his front leg and drives it to the covers, attempting to penetrate the off side field. Is still unable to do that as of now.

Kraigg Brathwaite's on side play is much stronger and better than his off side. The reason for this, as observed by Ian Bishop, is that he is a strong bottom-handed player and hence finds it easier to play deliveries to the leg side. Shai Hope, on the other hand is equally adept at playing on both side of the wickets. He concludes saying that it is not to suggest that one is better than the other as both have been scoring runs consistently.
Looped up on off, pushed right back to the bowler.
Bowls it just around the off stump line, Shai Hope defends it down on the off side.
Spinning in on middle and off, comfortably buried down on the track in front of him.
Full ball which is driven towards the mid off region. No run taken.
Straighter one on middle and leg, Brathwaite with minimal foot movement blocks it down under his nose.
Some decent drift for Raza, going away on middle stump, Kraigg stands firm and defends.
Works it with the turn and places it just in front of short leg.
Short, flat and outside leg, Brathwaite pulls it through the right of FSL for a double.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Hope leans ahead to the full ball and knocks it to mid off.
Landed outside off, guarded out from the back foot.
Lovely drive, connected well but is unfortunate it went straight to the fielder. With a beautiful extension of the arms Hope brought out the cover drive, only to be unable to pierce the gap.
Pushed slightly quicker through the air and outside off, Hope off the back foot keeps it out on the off side.
Loopy leg spinner outside off, driven to the cover fielder.
Stays right behind the line and keeps it out safely.
Not much spin on this occasion, full in line of the stumps, met with a straight bat.
Floats it right up there, around off, pushed away off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On middle and leg, worked away to mid-wicket.

Lbw appeal straight up! From around the wicket, it's darted really full around leg. Catches Brathwaite on the pads on his attempted sweep shot and there's a loud shout. Nothing from the umpire though, pitched outside the line of leg stump.
Sikandar Raza is into the attack. He has a slip and a short leg in place.
Flighted ball outside off, Hope with a push to the covers finds the man positioned there. Dot ball to end the over.
Spinning away from a driving length, Hope comes forward but only offers a block in response.
Looped up nicely outside off, eased back down towards mid off for an easy one.
A little short in length again, worked away to mid-wicket once more but this time it's too close to the fielder.
Dropped short on the stumps, Hope goes deep and works the pull towards mid-wicket for a run.
Wrong 'un around off, spinning in, Shai Hope is solid in defense.
Swinging back in from around off, on a bit of a fuller length, Brathwaite meets it with the full face of the bat.
Goes full again, it's defended easily from the front foot.

FOUR! Short again, trying to peg Brathwaite back but it doesn't bounce much at all. He goes back, moves inside the line and tickles it fine down the leg side. Malcolm Waller at fine leg runs to his right and tries to stop it with a dive, but fails in his attempt to do so.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Fuller in length and around that off stump line, Kraigg comes half-forward to push it back down the track.
Bit short in length, outside off, not much on that from the deck as Brathwaite deals with it rather easily.
There he is, using the depth of the crease to his advantage. Works it off the back foot on the leg side.
Works it against the spin past FSL for nothing.
Quick again, surprisingly not much flight from Graeme Cremer. Hope moves across his sticks to get behind the line and blocks.
Straighter one outside off, another defensive shot presented by the batsman.
Quicker outside off, Hope uses the depth of the crease well. Gives himself time by going back and defends it back down the track.
Flat, short and quick on middle and leg, worked away off the back foot to mid-wicket for a run.
Fullish in length pitched outside off, Hope brings a straight bat down in defense.
Full ball reversing an appreciable amount, Brathwaite flicks it to mid-wicket and picks up a quick single.
Full and well outside off, a bit slower in pace, the batsman reaches out to it and defends it on the on side from the inner half.
Good length ball shaping away a shade from around off, Kraigg opens the face of the bat and taps it in front of point.
Keeps it nice and straight. Fuller in length, it's pushed back in the bowler's direction.
Immediately makes it come back into the batsman, Brathwaite stands his ground and defends it down on the leg side.
Kyle Jarvis will bowl from the other end. He bowled with good purpose in the first session. Can he replicate it now or do better?
Served in line of the stumps, Shai lunges forward to defend.
Shai Hope goes back to this one to keep it out safely.
Flatter trajectory in line of the stumps, Brathwaite goes back and works it through mid-wicket for one run.
Fuller around off, pushed towards covers.
Turn and bounce there. Cremer floats it outside off, Kraigg watches it go into the keeper's gloves.
Floats it around off, Brathwaite lunges forward to block it.

Welcome back! The Windies are just bossing around both, the Zimbabwe bowlers as well as the tricky conditions. The hosts would want to put up a fight and for that, they need to be on the mark on the field. Will Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope, who walk out to resume their innings, continue to keep the bowlers at bay? Graeme Cremer will start the proceedings with the ball. A slip and short leg in place.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

Another good session for the tourists! They will be happy having just lost the one wicket of Kyle Hope in this morning session. With 67 runs being scored, the lead has now swelled up to 215 and all signs point towards the visitors racking up a big target for Zimbabwe. The home side could have gone into the break a happier bunch, had Kraigg Brathwaite not been dropped twice off skipper Graeme Cremer's bowling. He has already scored a fifty and will want to kick on. If early wickets are not taken in the post-lunch session, the game could very well slip out of the hands of the hosts. Join us for the second session in a while.
Floated around middle and leg, Brathwaite works it in front of square on the leg side and collects a run. That's Lunch, Day 3!
Waller lands it short around off, Hope goes back to pull it through square leg for a run.
Floated gently around leg, turned through mid-wicket for one run.
Brathwaite flicks this towards leg slip from the crease.
Shai Hope plays it towards mid on and crosses over to the other end.
Waller floats it on the pads, Hope taps it towards leg slip.
Shortish around off, cut away to point.
Kraigg strides forward and blocks it firmly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Brathwaite drives it to mid on.
Floated in line of the stumps, blocked off the front foot.
This ball is pushed towards covers from the crease.

FOUR! Waller offers a gift, Hope accepts it gleefully. Waller fires it short around leg, Shai goes back and pulls it through square leg for a boundary. It wasn't too far from the head of the short leg.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Shai keeps it out from within the crease.
Hope is watching the ball nicely as he goes back to this one and clips it towards short fine leg.
This ball is flicked towards mid-wicket.
Starts off round the wicket and serves it on the pads. Brathwaite goes back to clip it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Malcolm Waller to have a bowl now.
Floated full around leg, Kraigg flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.

Dropped! Would you believe it? Brathwaite is the beneficiary yet again and Chakabva the culprit. Cremer tosses this beautifully around middle and leg, Brathwaite lunges forward to block but gets a thin outside edge towards the keeper, who fluffs it. He went at it with hard hands and hence faltered. The skipper of Zimbabwe is doing his bit to create chances but he isn't getting support from the fielders. Kraigg bats on.
Floated in line of the stumps, Kraigg blocks it off the front foot.
FOUR! Bottom hand of Brathwaite comes into play there. Cremer tosses it around off, Kraigg allows it to pitch and drives it straight down the ground. Mid on gives it a chase but to no avail.
Shai goes back to this one and works it towards wide mid on. He crosses over to the other end.
Flighted full ball around middle and leg, Hope drives it towards mid off.
Again a harmless delivery outside off, moves in after pitching. Brathwaite has nothing to do with it and lets it go.
Shorter length around off, Shai stays back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
On a length outside off, Hope shoulders arms and lets it go.
Hurled in line of the stumps, Brathwaite flicks it through square leg and takes a run.
This delivery is driven back towards the bowler.
Fuller around off, driven towards covers.
Brathwaite drives it towards long off for a run.
Brathwaite gets behind the line of the ball and defends it.
Landed in line of the stumps, bunted off the front foot.
This ball is blocked off the front foot onto the ground.
Fuller around off, driven to mid off.

Dropped! Masakadza grasses one here! Cremer tosses it up outside off, Brathwaite lunges forward to defend but gets a thick outside edge. The ball goes low towards the right of slip, where Masakadza dives. He has a second go at it but still fails to cling on. Brathwaite survives. How costly will this be?
Served around middle and leg, Hope works it through backward square leg and hares back for the second.
Gets straighter and bowls it around middle and leg, Brathwaite clips it towards fine leg for one run.
Bowled outside off, Kraigg pushes it towards covers.
The Zimbabwe team physio is out in the middle. He is seen giving some tablets to Mire. It's very hot out there and that might be affecting the bowler.
Mire hurls it on a length outside off, Brathwaite shoulders arms to that. The ball goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Landed outside off, Kraigg pushes it towards covers.
Starts off with a length ball outside off, Brathwaite stands tall and blocks it to the off side.
Solomon Mire is brought into the attack. He showed how capable he is with the ball in the first innings with the wicket of Kyle Hope. He had bowled very good lines then. Can he repeat it?
Brathwaite drives it to long off for a run.
Loopy ball in line of the stumps, blocked solidly from the crease.
Cremer lands it on a shorter length around off, Hope goes back and pulls it towards wide mid on. One run taken.
Bowled outside off, Shai shows no intentions of playing it.
Floated around off, driven towards covers.
Flatter on the pads, he flicks it away towards short fine leg.
Fuller delivery, driven to the fielder at mid on.
This ball is punched through covers for a run.

Edged! Just short of the keeper! Mpofu bowls an off cutter on a length outside off. Hope hangs back to cut it again. Gets an outside edge but the ball lands just in front of Chakabva behind the stumps. Mpofu cannot believe his luck there.
FOUR! Lovely shot that! Length delivery just outside off, Hope puts his weight on the back foot and cuts it brilliantly through backward point. The ball is well timed and it races away to the fence.
Fuller around off and middle, Brathwaite clips it towards wide mid on and sprints across for a single.
Fuller outside off, Brathwaite drives it to covers.
Hope negotiates this safely by flicking it towards square leg from the crease.
This ball is driven to the cover fielder.
Served around off, Hope covers his stumps, allows the ball to turn and shoulders arms.
Floated full in line of the stumps, Hope drives it back to the bowler.
Hope goes back to this one and punches it to covers.
Looped full around middle and leg, Brathwaite flicks it towards mid-wicket and crosses over to the other end.
Similar delivery and sequence of actions like the previous ball.
Fuller outside off, left alone by Shai.
On a length outside off, Shai pushes it defensively towards point.
Mpofu bowls it full around off and gets it to shape in a bit. Brathwaite does well to play it in front of square on the on side for a run.
Hurled outside off, Brathwaite taps it towards covers.
Landed around off, Kraigg stays in the crease and defends that.
This ball is kept out with a solid forward defense.
Shorter outside off, Hope stays back and cuts it towards point.
This ball is played through mid on for a run.
Cleverly, Hope flicks it towards wide mid on for a single.

FOUR! Cremer certainly wouldn't be happy with the way he bowled that. Serves a long hop around middle and off, Hope goes back and pulls it over mid-wicket. Gets it off the bottom part of his bat and hence gets a boundary. Shai is miffed with himself as he missed out on a certain biggie there.
Floats it outside off, Hope drives it to covers.
Graeme Cremer is coming on to bowl now. Although Williams, who he replaces, troubled the batsman, that didn't translate into a wicket. The skipper would want to rectify that.
Shai drives it towards long on for a single.
This is too wide to make Hope play.
This pitch isn't easy to bat on for a new batsman. Shai Hope is finding that out with every passing minute. That's why it was even more imperative for a set Kyle Hope to carry on longer.
Landed in line of the stumps, blocked off the front foot.
Speared outside off, Hope drives it towards covers.
Hope gets behind the line of the ball and defends it solidly.

No Mpofu, don't bowl there! He serves a half volley around middle, Brathwaite is too good to miss out on such opportunities. He clips it nicely through mid-wicket and gets three as the ball slows down before the ropes.
Hope gets nicely forward to defend it onto the ground.
Another delivery outside off, left alone.
Flatter outside off, Hope covers the stumps and doesn't play at that.

Just over! Williams floats it outside off, Hope looks to cut it but is early into the shot. The ball bounces a bit more and catches the top edge that flies over the leaping cover fielder. No damage done. This was much like Chakabva's dismissal in the first innings. Only difference being that this flew over covers while the dismissal was at backward point.
During the drinks break, one member of the groundstaff was hammering down the landing area of the bowler to settle it.
Bowled outside off, Shai doesn't bother to play it.
Williams bowls it outside off, the ball stays low even as it spins. Hope looks to cut it but gets a bottom edge to the off side.

Allan Wilkins informs that Max Walker, the Australian fast bowler used to have different grip for every single ball he bowled in his first two overs to figure out what was the best way to go about it. He also adds that the great Andy Roberts too struggled to control the swing on the new ball and hence often used to hold it on the side to have better control.
This ball is pushed back towards the bowler.
Length ball outside off, Brathwaite stays in the crease and defends it towards point.
This ball is driven towards mid on.
Shorter outside off, Brathwaite's cut finds the point fielder.
Hurled outside off, driven towards covers.
Mpofu bowls it full outside off, Brathwaite lets it be.

Drinks break! The visitors continue to crawl ahead in the game. Jarvis was going through a very good spell in the morning, making use of the reverse swing to good effect. Kraigg Brathwaite and Kyle Hope did well to negotiate that for a major period till the pitch helped in bringing the latter's downfall. Zimbabwe would now look to make use of this opening to prize out some more scalps. Chris Mpofu will bowl for the first time today.
Bowled in line of the stumps, Shai lunges forward and blocks it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Now he knocks this towards long on for a run.

14th Test fifty for Kraigg Brathwaite. It has been a good knock from him. Windies needed someone to bat sensibly to extend their lead and the opener has done just that. He shouldn't think that his job is over yet and should look to carry on. Coming to the ball, it was looped up around middle and leg, Brathwaite flicked it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Landed on the pads, Kraigg flicks it towards square leg.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The silly point moves to short leg now.
This ball is flicked away off his pads.
Brathwaite flicks it towards mid-wicket. But a misfield there allows him a run. Zimbabwe need to be tidier on the field.

Ian Bishop on-air is comparing his bowling style with someone like Waqar Younis. He says that while he relied on his height and bowled it short, Younis used to aim for the yorker every ball. Hence the latter was a better exponent of the reverse swing as he bowled it fuller as opposed to Bishop who used to bowl on a back of a length.
This delivery in line of the stumps is blocked from the crease.
Length delivery down the leg side, Kraigg doesn't play at that and lets it go.
On a length around middle and leg, Hope nudges it down to fine leg for a single.
On a length outside off, Shai taps it towards cover-point.
Bowled in line of the stumps, Kraigg strides forward and blocks it.
Fuller around off, Shai drives it through mid off to get off the mark with a run.
Shai goes back and pushes it towards point.
Floated outside off, Hope looks to play at that but misses due to the spin there.
Brathwaite drives it towards long off and takes a run.
Served in line of the stumps, Kraigg goes back to block it from the crease.
Fuller around off, driven straight back to the bowler.

Jaffa first up! Jarvis bowls it on a length just outside off, Shai expects the ball to nip back in and plays for that. But this one moves just a touch to beat the outside edge of the bat. Kyle Jarvis is getting the ball to talk here!
Shai Hope replaces his brother Kyle Hope at the crease. He is going through a good run of form and would look to pile up some more runs under his belt.

OUT! Jarvis' efforts reap rewards, finally! He spears it outside off, the ball reverses into the batsman. Kyle Hope misses the flick and gets hit on the pads. The Zimbabweans appeal and the umpire upholds that. Hope has a chat with his partner about the review but is told to continue walking back. To be fair to him, he expected the ball to get up but it stayed low. Reverse swing combined with low bounce helps the hosts break the 82-run stand. Kyle Hope walks back after registering his best Test score, he would have wished to carry on though.
Cremer is not happy with the shape of the ball and approaches the umpire, who checks it with the help of 8-shaped gauge and reckons that all's good to continue.
Jarvis changes his length and bangs it short around off. Brathwaite is caught by surprise yet does well to jump and tuck it towards fine leg for a run.
Speared outside off, Kraigg shoulders arms and lets it be.
Fuller outside off, Hope taps it towards mid off and sets off for a run. The fielder hurls a wild throw at the keeper's end which misses Chakabva and goes towards fine leg. No extra run though.
Flatter in line of the stumps, the batsman goes back and gets a soft edge towards point.

A stat that will not please the fans of Zimbabwe. They suffered the second worst 9-wicket collapse in Tests, losing nine wickets for just 68 runs. Has it cost them the game already? They will hope not.
Brathwaite gets forward and defends it with a straight bat.
Landed around off and middle, Kraigg again pushes it defensively towards the bowler.
Looped up in line of the stumps, pushed back to the bowler.
Floated fuller around off, Kyle drives it to long off and crosses over to the other end.
Served around off, Hope goes back and guides it towards short third man.
This is bowled around off and middle, Kraigg gets nicely behind and defends it with a straight bat.
Similar delivery again, Brathwaite is having some trouble with this. Again gets it off the inner half to short leg.

Close again! Jarvis is using the reverse swing to good effect here. He hurls it around middle, Brathwaite gets it off the inner half of the bat again. It goes agonisingly past the deepish short leg fielder to mid-wicket.
Defends this delivery towards mid on.

Hurled around middle, Brathwaite gets it off the inner half of the bat. It goes through the forward short leg fielder and races away through mid-wicket. He gets a brace. To be fair to the fielder there, he didn't have any time to react to that.
Jarvis lands it fuller around off, Brathwaite gets nicely forward and pushes it to mid off. A hint of reverse swing there.
This ball is flicked towards square leg.
Served around off, Kyle gets forward and smothers it onto the ground.
Hope stays back and keeps it out from the crease.
Hope gets solidly behind that and blocks it onto the ground.
Again the spiteful spin on display. Williams tosses it up generously around off and middle, Hope lunges forward but finds the ball turn past the edge of the bat. Lovely delivery.
Floated in line of the stumps, Brathwaite nudges it towards short fine leg for a run.

Beautifully bowled! It is on a length just outside off, Hope pushes at it but gets beaten. The ball nipped away ever so slightly to beat the edge of the bat. This is a good line and length to persist with.
Fuller ball outside off, Kyle gets nicely forward and drives it to mid off.
Nicely bowled. Full delivery around middle and leg, Hope does well to dig it out towards the bowler.
Straight outside off, Hope shoulders arms to leave it alone.
Length delivery around off, Hope stands where he is and tries to punch it. Ends up playing it onto his pads. A puff of dust is seen after the ball pitched.
Served on a length outside off, Brathwaite defends it with half a mind. Gets it off the outer half of the bat towards cover-point for a run.
Hope stays back to keep this out safely.
This ball is pushed back towards the bowler.
Loopy delivery around off, Hope looks to defend but gets it off the inner half onto the ground.
100 up for Windies! This is floated around off, Hope cover drives it. The fielder there dives but is unable to get to the ball. A couple of runs taken.
This delivery around off is driven through covers for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Big appeal but the umpire shows no interest. Bowled on a length around off, Hope is stuck in the crease as he looks to flick. Gets hit on the pad which draws a huge shout. The umpire is unmoved. The hosts think of a review but decide against it. The ball would have gone over the stumps, as shown by Hawk Eye. Good decision.
While stealing the run there, Brathwaite was seen running in the danger area. He needs to be careful there.
Hurled on a length around off, Kyle gets nicely behind that and defends it next to the pitch on the leg side.
On a length around off, Hope stays in the crease and bunts it.

Well run! Similar delivery, Brathwaite taps it towards mid on and sees that Mire is late in getting to it. Steals a quick single by haring to the other end. The fielder mimes a throw to the keeper's end.
Pitched further up to the batsman, Brathwaite gets forward but gets it off the inner half towards mid on.
Landed in line of the stumps, Kraigg flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Hope goes back to this and hits it towards mid-wicket.
Floated around off, Hope stays back and hurriedly gets it towards point. The ball did not get up there.
Hope covers the line and flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Flighted fuller around off, Hope defends it getting forward.

FOUR! Don't ball short on this track. It won't fetch you wickets but will leak runs. Williams serves a half-tracker around middle, Hope is quick to go back and pull it over mid-wicket for a boundary. That's the first of the day.
Tossed up around off, Hope watchfully blocks it off the front foot.
Fuller again on the same line, Kraigg pushes it defensively towards mid-wicket.
Fuller around off and middle, Brathwaite gets forward and defends it towards mid-wicket.

It was interesting to note that in the 1st innings, Sean Williams talked about squeezing the runs which led to the Windies batsmen struggling and it resulted in a collapse. Zimbabwe were guilty of giving away too many runs too easily yesterday. Looks like they have gone back to the 'Give no runs' plan and are keeping things tight.
Bowled on the pads, Hope gets it off the inner half towards fine leg for a run.
Speared straight on a length, Hope misses the flick and wears it high on the thigh pads.
Full outside off, Kyle doesn't bother putting bat to that.
Hurled on a length around off, Hope stays back and blocks it towards covers.
Bowled in line of the stumps, the batsman defends it off the front foot.

Served around off, Brathwaite gets forward to defend but gets an edge that dies towards the slip. He needs to forget this ball and continue to play normally as such deliveries will keep coming on such a track.
Floated around off and middle, Kraigg gets nicely forward and defends.
Kraigg lunges forward to smother the spin.
Flatter in line of the stumps, Brathwaite goes back to flick it away but gets a leading edge past silly point.
Beaten once again. Lovely loopy ball around off, Brathwaite lunges forward to play for the initial angle but the ball spins away to beat the edge of his bat.
Similar delivery, Kyle pushes it towards mid-wicket off the front foot.
Fuller around off and middle, Hope clips it with the angle through mid-wicket and collects a brace.

That stayed low! The pitch has started playing mischief already. Jarvis bowls it on a length outside off, Hope plays for the length. The ball refuses to get up and passes under his bat and goes through to the keeper. Good for the batsman that the ball wasn't in line of the stumps. Not good signs these for the hosts, who have to bat last here.
On a length outside off, Hope goes back and defends it towards point.
Length outside off, Brathwaite punches it through cover-point for a run.
Begins with a delivery around off, Brathwaite blocks it towards mid-wicket.
Kyle Jarvis to run in from the other end. A slip and a gully in position for him.
Fuller around off, pushed off the front foot towards covers. A maiden to start the day.
This ball is cut away towards cover-point.
Vicious turn again! Tossed up around middle, Hope strides forward to block but the ball spins away sharply.
Williams is lucky to get away with that. Shorter outside off, Hope finds the cover fielder with the slap.
Straighter one outside off, Kyle shoulders arms to let that go.
Turn straightaway! Lands it around off, Hope comes half-forward to defend. But the ball spins away past the edge of the bat.

Everybody is set for play to get underway. The overnight unbeaten pair of Brathwaite and Hope stride out to bat. Can they prolong the good work done so far? The hosts would like to end the adamant approach of the batters. Sean Williams to have a go first up. A slip and a silly point in place.

Tino Mawoyo doing the pitch report reckons the conditions are good for spinners and there's a little bit of breeze across the ground. Adds there are lots of cracks on the surface, it's drying up and the off spinners, especially, can attack the batsmen and cause problems. Opines that the West Indies batsmen used their feet well to get to the pitch and negate the spin yesterday. Ends by saying that Zimbabwe have their work cut out today.

Looking at the turn on offer, Zimbabwe wouldn't hope against skittling out the visitors as quickly as possible. However, rather than letting the pitch play the part, the hosts were guilty of trying a bit too hard, thereby being undisciplined. They would do well to learn from that and be on the money right away. Stay with us to see if Zimbabwe can make a comeback.

Welcome to Day 3 of the 1st Test between Zimbabwe and Windies in Bulawayo. Both teams have had a day to their credit in the game. The tourists have wrested back the initiative, courtesy their bowling and hence are on top at the moment. They would look to drive home the advantage and extend their lead, which stands at 148 currently, to anything over 300. The current pair of Kraigg Brathwaite and Kyle Hope is already on the right track with an unbeaten half century stand.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

West Indies will be delighted with their work. Devendra Bishoo led the fightback with a five-wicket haul that ensured his side got a 60-run lead. Despite losing Kieran Powell to Graeme Cremer, the tourists are right on top thanks to the stand between Kraigg Brathwaite and Kyle Hope. The hosts were too eager with the ball as well and it showed in their poor bowling. The lead is reaching 150 and the hosts would know anything over 250 on this wicket could mean trouble. Should be another fighting day of Test cricket. Join us for all the action on Day 3 tomorrow at 1000 local (0800 GMT). Until then, it's goodbye and take care.

What an enthralling day of Test cricket! Zimbabwe began the day right on top but now are lagging behind in the game. They have nobody but themselves to blame for this though. After having bowled out the tourists for a low score, they needed to bat with application and determination but they let themselves down with some ordinary cricket. Nobody cared to apply on this wicket apart from Craig Ervine and the result is for all to see.
Fuller outside off, driven back to the bowler by Brathwaite. What a day it has been! That's Stumps, Day 2!
Last ball of the day!
Hurls it around off, Brathwaite goes back and defends it watchfully.
Flatter around off, Brathwaite stays back and gets it off the outer half towards the off side.
Shorter around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter around off, Hope goes back and defends it.
Lands it around leg, spins down, Hope looks to turn it away but is beaten. The keeper does well to collect it despite the turn on that one.
Last over of the day!
Lands it around middle, Brathwaite comes ahead and blocks it.
Fuller around off, Brathwaite gets right forward and defends it.
Nudges one towards mid-wicket and takes a single.
Too full around off, pushed towards covers by the batsman.
Hope comes right forward and blocks this one.
Bowls it around off, Kyle defends it from his crease.
Flatter around middle, KB goes back and turns it towards square leg.
Shorter around off, Brathwaite keeps it out.
Kraigg comes down to hit one but is almost yorked. He does well to pat it back down the wicket.
Shorter outside off, punched towards covers by Brathwaite.
This one is nudged towards mid-wicket by Kraigg.
Bowls it around middle, Brathwaite comes down the wicket and tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Shorter outside leg, worked to long leg for a single by Brathwaite.
This time Kyle neatly turns one through mid-wicket for a single.
Too full around off, Kyle looks to keep it out but gets an inside edge onto his boot. He picked the googly there.
Cremer bowls it outside leg, Hope stands tall and lets the ball hit his pads.
Bowl it in the same area, Brathwaite works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Lands it outside leg, Brathwaite pads it away. Interesting tactic, negative? Maybe.

Stays back to turn one through the leg side but almost hits it into the hands of the waiting leg slip fielder. A single taken as the ball goes wide of the fielder. Things happening but a little too late in the day, not that the hosts will mind. The lead is now 143 runs.
Brathwaite comes forward and blocks this one.
Bowls it flatter around leg, Brathwaite lunges forward to defend but hits it in the air towards short leg. Ervine cannot get to the ball in time. You need to make most of such chances.
Full and outside off, driven to mid off.
Lands it around middle, Brathwaite looks to defend but gets hit on his pads. A stifled appeal is turned down.
Goes round the wicket and bowls it around leg, turned towards square leg.
Short again, they have bowled far too many of them. Kyle has enough time to go back and punch it to covers.
Quicker around off, Kyle comes right forward and keeps it out.
FOUR! Kyle goes BOOM! Shorter outside off, Hope goes way back in the crease and lofts it over mid-wicket. There is no one in the deep and Kyle gets a boundary. This is now his highest Test score!
Fuller around off, Hope comes forward and blocks it.
Lands it just outside off, spins away, Kyle covers the line well and defends it.
Shorter in length around off, Hope goes back and pulls it to mid-wicket.
Change of ends for Graeme Cremer!
Lands it shorter around middle, Brathwaite tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Hope slinks down the wicket and turns it to long on for a single.
Similar ball, this time Hope carefully turns it towards the square leg fielder.
Flatter outside off, spins in, Hope stays back and turns it towards the leg side.
Shorter in length, spins in, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller outside off, Hope comes down the wicket and turns it through mid on for a single.
Comes right forward and blocks this one.
Around the pads, turned towards the leg side by Kraigg.
Shorter outside off, punched to covers.
Fuller around middle, Brathwaite clips it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs. 50-run stand up comes up between the two and it is an important one in context of the game.
Short and outside off, punched to point by the batsman.
Brathwaite comes forward and pushes it towards covers.
Kyle comes down the wicket and burries this one into the wicket.
SHARP TURN! Raza lands it outside off, gets it to come in sharply. Brathwaite looking to punch does well to keep it out of danger with a closed face of the bat. A single taken.
Quicker around middle, worked through square leg for a single. Zimbabwe spinners are trying too hard here.
Kyle Hope comes forward and defends it off his pads.
Fires it around off and middle, Hope keeps it out.
Flatter around off, Hope stays back and defends it.
That keeps happening! Williams bowls it just in that area outside off, Brathwaite prods forward to defend but does so in the air yet again. The silly point fielder cannot reach it.
Fuller around leg, Kraigg looks to turn it through but does not connect it well.
Short and outside off, punched towards covers by Brathwaite.
Brathwaite comes forward and turns it towards mid-wicket.
Fuller around off, pushed off the outer half towards short third man for a single.
Fuller around middle, Hope digs it out back down the wicket.
Fires it around leg, Brathwaite looks to clip it away but fails to connect. The keeper takes the ball and looks to whip the bails off but Kraigg never left the crease completely.
Wrong line, on the pads, and Kyle nudges it through square leg for a single.
Extra fielder in place at mid-wicket for the chip in the air.
FOUR! Kyle takes it on! Knows that Raza is not a threatening bowler and hence comes down the wicket and whacks one over mid-wicket for a boundary. Good intent by the Windies no 3.
Flatter on the pads, worked through short fine leg for a couple.
Hope comes down and looks to bunt one through mid-wicket, does not beat the fielder.
Flatter around off, Hope defends it from his crease.
Bowling change, Sikandar Raza called on for a bowl.
Too full on middle and leg, Kraigg keeps it out.
Fuller around off, Brathwaite pushes it in the air towards silly point.
Works it towards mid-wicket from his crease.
Short and wide outside off, Brathwaite cuts it square of the wicket. Raza hares after it from point and stops it from going through. Two runs taken.
Brathwaite comes forward and defends this one.
Flatter around middle, worked towards mid-wicket by Brathwaite.
Shorter outside off, punched through covers for a single.
Comes forward and drives it nicely towards mid off.
Flatter around leg, nudged through backward square leg for a couple of runs.
Full around leg, Kyle comes down and pushes it to long on for a single.
Loops it outside off, Hope comes forward and defends it.
Shorter around middle, worked towards mid-wicket.
Angles it around off, Brathwaite lunges forward to defend it.
Too full outside off, driven off the front foot by Kraigg.
Works one through backward square leg for another brace.
Shorter outside off, Brathwaite rides the bounce and taps it.
Too full on the pads, turned through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Fuller around middle, turned towards mid on by Brathwaite.
Flatter outside off, another googly, Hope defends it off his back foot.
Floats it around off, Hope comes forward and blocks it.
Fuller around off, kept out by Kyle.
Hope prods forward and pushes one towards silly point.
Fuller around off, Kyle comes down and pushes it towards covers.
Googly outside off, spins in, Hope plays for the conventional turn and hence gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Edged! Bowls it around off, Brathwaite lunges forward to defend but gets an outside edge towards short third man.
